description: Normative list of everything a GHOST relay is permitted to observe per event (threat model v2.1 section 6, ADR-09). Any field not listed here is a privacy violation. Values are opaque identifiers, buckets or coarse times; never IPs, identities, plaintext or free text. A field with `ops` may appear only on events whose `op` is one of them. Version 2 (Phase 9 design §4.7, §10.2; ADR-30, ADR-32): op `register`, field `key_kind`, `ttl_bucket_seconds` in place of `ttl_bucket_days`.

blob_hash.note: SHA-256 of the exact ciphertext blob

time_bucket.note: unix seconds rounded down to the minute

ttl_bucket_seconds.note: exact TTL bucket of a store; the relay refuses any other TTL (ADR-32)

key_kind.note: register events only (ADR-30; fetch per design §22.8.7)

period_id.note: public token validity period; on register, the ISO week the registration names

capability_scope.note: SHA-256 of the presented credential: a write capability, or a bearer read, deposit or fetch credential v3 (ADR-30; fetch per design §22.8.7); never the credential itself

request_id.note: client idempotency key, random per request

circuit_id.note: relay-local id of the onion circuit; never an IP

result.note: rejected_token: a redeemed token is malformed, forged, of another kind, slot or key, or revoked; rejected_period: a token outside its acceptance window or of a closed period (ADR-25, Phase 8 design §10.6), or a registration for a week other than its capability's week or the next (ADR-30); rejected_ttl: a store whose TTL is not exactly a bucket or exceeds the relay's maximum (ADR-32)
